title: Understanding the File·pathlib·encoding Workflow
body: Path makes path composition and inspection convenient and portable, but it does not make a path secure. Check the working directory, existence and kind, permissions, encoding, overwrite policy, and read/write exceptions.
examples: Construct the path as follows: Path('data') / 'input.txt'.
Use `read_text(encoding='utf-8')` to safely read Korean text.

title: Understanding the Object-Method-Class Flow
body: Class code is read as a way to see what data and behaviors an object possesses.
detail: An object is an actual entity created based on a class. A method is an action that an object can perform, and `self` refers to the object itself. When reading class code, check what state is stored in the constructor and whether methods read or modify that state. In particular, methods that modify internal state—such as those for lists or dictionaries—can have side effects, so you must also observe the changes before and after they are called.
examples: Distinguish between methods that simply return a value and those that directly modify the object's state.

title: Understanding the Packaging and Dependency Flow
body: venv and requirements are basic tools for isolation and installation requirements. Strong reproduction may also require Python and OS constraints, direct and transitive pins, a lock or hashes, and a verification command. The environment interpreter can be invoked directly without activation.
examples: Create a project-specific virtual environment using `python -m venv .venv`.
Install the required packages using `python -m pip install -r requirements.txt`.

title: Understanding the Metadata, Deduplication, and Integrity Workflow
body: In data processing, the reliability of the results is verified through deduplication, joins, and integrity checks.
detail: Metadata is information that describes the data itself. For example, values such as source, creation date, file name, and ID can be considered metadata. Deduplication is the process of removing duplicates to ensure that the same item is not included multiple times. Joins and SQL are used to link multiple tables, but if the keys are incorrect, rows may be lost or duplicated. Therefore, after processing, you must verify the count, check for missing rows, identify duplicates, and ensure key integrity.
examples: Remove duplicate rows based on the `item_id`.
Check whether the number of rows has suddenly increased or decreased after the join.

title: Understanding the PWA, Cache, and LocalStorage Workflow
body: PWAs manage state and cache so that web apps function seamlessly even when offline or during subsequent visits.
detail: PWA-related code is often structured to store app files in the cache and save the user’s progress in a storage mechanism such as localStorage. The cache is a mechanism for quickly loading app resources or for use while offline, while localStorage is used to store small amounts of state, such as user preferences or learning progress. When reading the code, be sure to check the timing of storage and retrieval, as well as the conditions for updates.
examples: Store the ID of the last study card in localStorage.
A service worker caches the app files so they load quickly when the user returns to the site.

title: Understanding Automation, Workflow, and Git Workflows
body: Automation moves repeated work into scripts or CI. A Git flow commonly covers change, verification, staging, commit, and push; a tag is optional when a release checkpoint is needed. Separate mutations from checks and ensure a failed quality gate blocks publication.
examples: The code must pass validation before it can be committed.
We use GitHub Actions to automatically run tests to verify that quality standards are met.

title: Understanding the Architecture·Documentation Workflow
body: The architecture document serves as a roadmap that describes the project's components and the separation of responsibilities.
detail: When reviewing the architecture, check which modules are responsible for what and which layers the data passes through. Documentation doesn’t just describe how to use the system; it can also explain why a particular structure was chosen and guide you on which files to review first. In a service-oriented architecture, roles are divided into components such as the UI, API, storage, and batch jobs, so connecting the inputs and outputs of each part reveals the overall flow.
examples: Check the README for instructions on how to run the program and the main folder structure.
We will examine how the UI layer and the data layer are connected through certain functions.

title: Reading Float, Numeric, and NaN Flows
body: A float is a binary approximation, so decimal comparison and rounding need care. pandas NaN or NA marks missing data, is not simply an empty string, and may compare differently from ordinary numbers. Check conversion errors, missing-data policy, dtype, tolerances, and expected range.
examples: float('3.14') converts a string into a decimal number.
NaN values may need to be handled differently than regular numerical comparisons.
